title: Heterogeneous treatment effects by firm size in DID

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy
- Method: Difference-in-Differences (twoway fixed effects). Large firms (treated=1) receive a larger tax cut from period 4 onward; small firms (treated=0) receive a smaller, common tax cut. With firm and year fixed effects, the coefficient on treat_x_post identifies the differential effect on large firms’ investment relative to small firms, net of the common post-4 effect captured by year fixed effects.
- Parameter: β in y_it = α_i + γ_t + β·(treated_i × post_t) + ε_it. Because both groups are “treated” to some extent, β is the heterogeneous treatment effect: the incremental impact of the larger tax cut (large vs. small).
- Key assumptions:
  - Parallel trends in the absence of the differential tax change: after removing common time shocks (γ_t) and time-invariant firm heterogeneity (α_i), large and small firms would have evolved similarly.
  - No anticipation and stable composition; SUTVA (no spillovers across firms).

We assess the plausibility of parallel trends via an event-study (leads) and a pre-period placebo DID, and test robustness to group-specific linear trends and two-way clustering.

## 2. R Code
```r
# Complete, self-contained R code that:
# - Reads the CSV file from the path provided
# - Runs the appropriate causal analysis
# - Prints a clear numerical result (coefficient, CAR, etc.)
# - Includes basic robustness checks

# -----------------------
# 0) Setup
# -----------------------
suppressWarnings({
  has_fixest <- requireNamespace("fixest", quietly = TRUE)
  has_sandwich <- requireNamespace("sandwich", quietly = TRUE)
  has_lmtest <- requireNamespace("lmtest", quietly = TRUE)
  has_data_table <- requireNamespace("data.table", quietly = TRUE)
})

# Helper for clustered SE with base lm when fixest is unavailable
cluster_se_lm <- function(model, cluster_vec) {
  if (!has_sandwich || !has_lmtest) stop("sandwich and lmtest packages are required for clustered SE fallback.")
  vc <- sandwich::vcovCL(model, cluster = cluster_vec, type = "HC1")
  out <- lmtest::coeftest(model, vcov. = vc)
  return(out)
}

# Helper to print a clear numerical summary line
print_main_result <- function(est, se, pval, coef_name = "treat_x_post") {
  ci_low <- est - 1.96 * se
  ci_high <- est + 1.96 * se
  pct <- 100 * (exp(est) - 1)
  cat(sprintf("\nMain DID (heterogeneous effect, coef=%s):", coef_name))
  cat(sprintf("\n  Estimate (log points): %.4f", est))
  cat(sprintf("\n  Std. Error: %.4f", se))
  cat(sprintf("\n  95%% CI: [%.4f, %.4f]", ci_low, ci_high))
  cat(sprintf("\n  p-value: %.4g", pval))
  cat(sprintf("\n  Implied percent effect on investment: %.2f%%\n", pct))
}

# -----------------------
# 1) Read Data
# -----------------------
path <- "experiments/exp_b/data/s09_data.csv"
dat <- read.csv(path)

# Basic checks and prep
if (!"unit_id" %in% names(dat) || !"period" %in% names(dat) || !"treated" %in% names(dat) ||
    !"post" %in% names(dat) || !"treat_x_post" %in% names(dat) || !"y" %in% names(dat)) {
  stop("Required columns are missing.")
}
# Coerce to factors for FE (lm fallback) and for fixest FE indexing
dat$unit_id <- as.integer(dat$unit_id)
dat$period <- as.integer(dat$period)
dat$treated <- as.integer(dat$treated)
dat$post <- as.integer(dat$post)
dat$treat_x_post <- as.integer(dat$treat_x_post)

# Event-study relative time (policy starts at period 4)
event_time <- 4L
dat$rel_t <- dat$period - event_time

# -----------------------
# 2) Main DID (TWFE)
# -----------------------
if (has_fixest) {
  # fixest implementation with firm and year FE; unit-clustered SE
  mod_main <- fixest::feols(y ~ treat_x_post | unit_id + period, data = dat, cluster = ~ unit_id)
  ct <- fixest::coeftable(mod_main)
  est <- ct["treat_x_post", "Estimate"]
  se  <- ct["treat_x_post", "Std. Error"]
  pval <- ct["treat_x_post", "Pr(>|t|)"]
  print_main_result(est, se, pval, coef_name = "treat_x_post")
} else {
  # Fallback: lm with firm and year dummies; cluster-robust SE by unit
  mod_main <- lm(y ~ treat_x_post + factor(unit_id) + factor(period), data = dat)
  ct <- cluster_se_lm(mod_main, cluster_vec = dat$unit_id)
  # Extract
  rowname <- "treat_x_post"
  if (!(rowname %in% rownames(ct))) stop("Coefficient treat_x_post not found in the model output.")
  est <- ct[rowname, "Estimate"]
  se  <- ct[rowname, "Std. Error"]
  pval <- ct[rowname, "Pr(>|t|)"]
  print_main_result(est, se, pval, coef_name = "treat_x_post")
}

# -----------------------
# 3) Event-Study (pre-trends and dynamics of differential effect)
#     y_it = α_i + γ_t + Σ_k≠(-1) β_k [1(treated=1) × 1(rel_t=k)] + ε_it
#     Base period: rel_t = -1 (the year before policy)
# -----------------------
# Keep rel_t within observed range
rel_levels <- sort(unique(dat$rel_t))
# Build event-study either via fixest's i() or manual dummies
if (has_fixest) {
  mod_es <- fixest::feols(y ~ fixest::i(rel_t, treated, ref = -1) | unit_id + period,
                          data = dat, cluster = ~ unit_id)
  es_coefs <- stats::coef(mod_es)
  es_names <- names(es_coefs)
  # Print a concise set of post-period differential effects (k = 0 to 4 if available)
  cat("\nEvent-study (differential effects for large vs. small, relative to rel_t = -1):\n")
  for (k in 0:4) {
    nm_candidates <- grep(paste0("rel_t::", "\\(", k, "\\)"), es_names, value = TRUE)
    # In some fixest versions, names may differ; if not found, try alternative pattern
    if (length(nm_candidates) == 0) nm_candidates <- grep(paste0("rel_t\\.", k, ":treated"), es_names, value = TRUE)
    if (length(nm_candidates) > 0) {
      nm <- nm_candidates[1]
      se_k <- sqrt(vcov(mod_es)[nm, nm])
      est_k <- es_coefs[nm]
      cat(sprintf("  k=%d: est=%.4f, se=%.4f\n", k, est_k, se_k))
    }
  }
} else {
  # Manual ES: create interaction dummies for treated × rel_t = k, excluding k = -1
  rel_all <- sort(unique(dat$rel_t))
  rel_use <- rel_all[rel_all != -1]
  for (k in rel_use) {
    dat[[paste0("D_rel_", k)]] <- as.integer(dat$treated == 1L & dat$rel_t == k)
  }
  # Build formula: y ~ D_rel_k (for k != -1) + FE
  rhs <- paste(c(paste0("D_rel_", rel_use), "factor(unit_id)", "factor(period)"), collapse = " + ")
  f_es <- as.formula(paste("y ~", rhs))
  mod_es <- lm(f_es, data = dat)
  ct_es <- cluster_se_lm(mod_es, cluster_vec = dat$unit_id)
  cat("\nEvent-study (manual; differential effects for large vs. small, relative to rel_t = -1):\n")
  for (k in 0:4) {
    rn <- paste0("D_rel_", k)
    if (rn %in% rownames(ct_es)) {
      est_k <- ct_es[rn, "Estimate"]; se_k <- ct_es[rn, "Std. Error"]
      cat(sprintf("  k=%d: est=%.4f, se=%.4f\n", k, est_k, se_k))
    }
  }
}

# -----------------------
# 4) Robustness checks
#   (a) Two-way clustered SE (if fixest available)
#   (b) Group-specific linear trend
#   (c) Pre-policy placebo DID (pre-trend test on periods <= 3)
#   (d) Aggregated DID on group means (sanity check)
# -----------------------

# (a) Two-way clustering (unit_id and period) when available
if (has_fixest) {
  mod_main_tw <- fixest::feols(y ~ treat_x_post | unit_id + period, data = dat, cluster = ~ unit_id + period)
  ct_tw <- fixest::coeftable(mod_main_tw)
  est_tw <- ct_tw["treat_x_post", "Estimate"]
  se_tw  <- ct_tw["treat_x_post", "Std. Error"]
  p_tw   <- ct_tw["treat_x_post", "Pr(>|t|)"]
  ci_low_tw <- est_tw - 1.96 * se_tw
  ci_high_tw <- est_tw + 1.96 * se_tw
  cat("\nRobustness (two-way clustered SEs at unit and period):")
  cat(sprintf("\n  Estimate: %.4f, SE: %.4f, 95%% CI: [%.4f, %.4f], p-value: %.4g\n",
              est_tw, se_tw, ci_low_tw, ci_high_tw, p_tw))
}

# (b) Add group-specific linear trend (treated × period)
if (has_fixest) {
  mod_trend <- fixest::feols(y ~ treat_x_post + treated:period | unit_id + period, data = dat, cluster = ~ unit_id)
  ct_tr <- fixest::coeftable(mod_trend)
  est_tr <- ct_tr["treat_x_post", "Estimate"]
  se_tr  <- ct_tr["treat_x_post", "Std. Error"]
  p_tr   <- ct_tr["treat_x_post", "Pr(>|t|)"]
} else {
  mod_trend <- lm(y ~ treat_x_post + I(treated * period) + factor(unit_id) + factor(period), data = dat)
  ct_tr_mat <- cluster_se_lm(mod_trend, cluster_vec = dat$unit_id)
  est_tr <- ct_tr_mat["treat_x_post", "Estimate"]
  se_tr  <- ct_tr_mat["treat_x_post", "Std. Error"]
  p_tr   <- ct_tr_mat["treat_x_post", "Pr(>|t|)"]
}
ci_low_tr <- est_tr - 1.96 * se_tr
ci_high_tr <- est_tr + 1.96 * se_tr
cat("\nRobustness (add treated × period linear trend):")
cat(sprintf("\n  Estimate: %.4f, SE: %.4f, 95%% CI: [%.4f, %.4f], p-value: %.4g\n",
            est_tr, se_tr, ci_low_tr, ci_high_tr, p_tr))

# (c) Pre-policy placebo DID restricted to periods <= 3
dat_pre <- subset(dat, period <= 3)
dat_pre$post_fake <- as.integer(dat_pre$period >= 2)
dat_pre$treat_x_post_fake <- dat_pre$treated * dat_pre$post_fake
if (has_fixest) {
  mod_placebo <- fixest::feols(y ~ treat_x_post_fake | unit_id + period, data = dat_pre, cluster = ~ unit_id)
  ct_pl <- fixest::coeftable(mod_placebo)
  est_pl <- ct_pl["treat_x_post_fake", "Estimate"]
  se_pl  <- ct_pl["treat_x_post_fake", "Std. Error"]
  p_pl   <- ct_pl["treat_x_post_fake", "Pr(>|t|)"]
} else {
  mod_placebo <- lm(y ~ treat_x_post_fake + factor(unit_id) + factor(period), data = dat_pre)
  ct_pl_mat <- cluster_se_lm(mod_placebo, cluster_vec = dat_pre$unit_id)
  est_pl <- ct_pl_mat["treat_x_post_fake", "Estimate"]
  se_pl  <- ct_pl_mat["treat_x_post_fake", "Std. Error"]
  p_pl   <- ct_pl_mat["treat_x_post_fake", "Pr(>|t|)"]
}
ci_low_pl <- est_pl - 1.96 * se_pl
ci_high_pl <- est_pl + 1.96 * se_pl
cat("\nPlacebo DID in pre-periods (fake policy at period 2; sample: periods 1–3):")
cat(sprintf("\n  Estimate: %.4f, SE: %.4f, 95%% CI: [%.4f, %.4f], p-value: %.4g\n",
            est_pl, se_pl, ci_low_pl, ci_high_pl, p_pl))

# (d) Aggregated DID on group means (pre: 1–3, post: 4–8)
agg <- aggregate(y ~ treated + I(period <= 3) + I(period >= 4), data = dat, FUN = mean)
# Alternatively compute directly:
mean_y <- aggregate(y ~ treated + period, data = dat, FUN = mean)
pre_means <- aggregate(y ~ treated, data = subset(mean_y, period <= 3), FUN = mean)
post_means <- aggregate(y ~ treated, data = subset(mean_y, period >= 4), FUN = mean)
delta_large <- post_means[post_means$treated == 1, "y"] - pre_means[pre_means$treated == 1, "y"]
delta_small <- post_means[post_means$treated == 0, "y"] - pre_means[pre_means$treated == 0, "y"]
did_agg <- as.numeric(delta_large - delta_small)
cat("\nAggregated DID (difference of average log-changes, large minus small):")
cat(sprintf("\n  DID (log points): %.4f; Implied percent effect: %.2f%%\n",
            did_agg, 100 * (exp(did_agg) - 1)))
```

## 3. Expected Findings
- Sign: Positive. Large firms, benefiting from a larger tax cut, should increase investment more than small firms.
- Magnitude: In log terms, a differential effect around 0.05–0.15 (≈5–15%) is plausible, reflecting a sizable but realistic responsiveness of investment to net-of-tax cash flow/cost-of-capital changes. The event study should show near-zero and statistically insignificant pre-trend (leads), with a discrete jump from period 4 onward that persists or grows slightly. Robustness checks should yield similar estimates.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: DID with heterogeneous effects — triple-diff or interaction terms for size groups
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: Large firms increase investment more than small firms post tax cut
_ground_truth.main_effect: 28% higher investment growth for large firms
